Engineering note:
1. Ensure the focus is managed when the page dynamically changes (refer to the comment on the step 1 of the flow)
2. Image appears to be decorative
3. "Verify" button needs to have HTML `disabled` attribute while disabled and then the attribute should be removed dynamically, when the button is to become actionable
4. Input field has a couple of a11y considerations:
* "Enter phone number", in this case, is a `placeholder` attribute value while "Verify your phone number" could be either `<label for="input_id_ref">` or referred with `aria-labelledby` from this `<input>` and the subheading text "For your security..." could be referred with `aria-describedby`, so both are announced and the field is labeled.
* Since the phone of the user is considered to be a common field, using `autocomplete` attribute is highly encouraged - it would allow for an OS- and browser-provided autocomplete functionality to work. Use either `autocomplete="tel"` (if a country code is expected) or `autocomplete="tel-national"` (if a phone number without country code is expected) - refer to the input purpose indications for other options available.

Engineering note:
1. Ensure the focus is managed when the page dynamically changes (refer to the comment on the step 1 of the flow)
2. Ideally, both options would be marked up as radio buttons. But using ARIA radiogroup pattern is acceptable as well - just make sure the keyboard interaction is also provided (Tab to the pre-selected `role=radio` control and then use Up/Down arrows to change the selection ("aria-checked" value) while changing the focus between two options, then Tab to "Continue" button). 
3. 2a. In this case, the "Choose a recovery method" heading's `id` could be used for the `aria-labelledby` reference and the subheading text under it could be referred by `aria-describedby` - both ARIA attributes to be added on the wrapper of the heading+subheading+options group with `role=radiogroup` (example)
4. If using radiogroup is not possible, ensure each option including its description is a button with `aria-pressed` attribute, and that they both are wrapped in a group landmark (but this would create an unnecessary tab stop for keyboard users and unnecessary unavoidable verbosity for screen reader users)
5. Images look like decorative
6. If in doubt, reach out to the a11y team and allies in the #accessibility channel ;)

Engineering notes:
* Ideally, we'd mark the container of this non-modal dialog with `<main>` or `<article>` or `role="group"` and `aria-labelledby` set to the `id` of the "Connect another device" text element - or use another HTML element that creates a landmark, so when navigating in this area the screen reader user becomes aware that this is a structure.
* When the flow is opened, ideally, the focus would be placed on the `<main>` container or the `<-` Back button - the idea is to avoid screen reader users to hear the heading all over again and for keyboard users to avoid the need to tab through the header too. To place a focus on a container (non-interactive) element, use `tabindex="-1"` on it and place the focus with JS `focus()` method. 
* a. Focus should be managed on each dynamic update of the flow page (if the page is not fully reloading)
* b. Alternatively, if the page is refreshed on each step of the flow, we could provide a skiplink for keyboard users to get to the main area and skip the header (this, in general, is expected on all webpages)
* `<-` button has to be labeled, i.e. as `Back`
* Progress bar should either be using the role=progressbar and its associated ARIA attributes or HTML <progress> element (or <meter>, at least)
* Using ordered list markup (with visually hidden bullets) would be the best for the steps on the page.
* Ensure there is an alt text for the QR code. @Peter Benvenuto -  something like "QR code" should be sufficient, yet, some advice to add a location so a blind screen reader user could point their camera to an approximate position, i.e. "QR code (located in the middle of the screen)"
* Ensure the disabled button has HTML `disabled` attribute that is removed, when the input received-
